name: Shadow Mountain Designated Camping Area
note: Bridger-Teton NF designated undeveloped sites on Shadow Mountain, reached from US 26/89 by Antelope Flats Road on the east edge of Grand Teton NP; camping only at the marked, numbered sites. The base sites by the toilet are the easiest; the rest line the summit loop road, which the Forest Service calls rough in places and campers report muddy after rain. Larger rigs are best kept to the base sites; call the Jackson Ranger District about road conditions before setting out. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: Bridger-Teton NF camping page (read 2026-11-20), Jackson and Blackrock Designated Undeveloped Sites table: 'Shadow Mountain - No. First come, first served. - From Jackson, take Highway 26/89 north 13.3 miles and turn right at Antelope Flats Road. Continue 3.3 miles to the stop sign and turn left. Follow signs to the National Forest. - Sites at base of mountain fill quickly. Summit loop road is rough in places. Toilet at base. No water.'; Forest Order 04-03-24-204 Described Area D names the 'Shadow Mountain ... designated camping area' (Jackson RD); USFS road layer: FR 30340 SHADOW MOUNTAIN (7.14 mi loop) is maintenance level 3 'SUITABLE FOR PASSENGER CARS'; Esri imagery shows the base gravel loop at the pin with trailers/RVs parked and a toilet building; The Dyrt (87 reviews, 4.6): 26-ft Class C at site 18 (2024), small trailers and pop-ups 'without issue' (2023) -> agency-designated drive-in sites a 23-ft rig reaches (small free NF sites rule, call-first caveat). Not on recreation.gov (search 2026-11-20).
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-20: Esri World_Imagery (rendered) at 43.7002,-110.6168 (~250 m frame) and over the whole FR 30340 loop (~5 km frame, USFS road layer drawn on): the base sites are a gravel loop in sage/aspen on the lower slope and the summit-loop sites sit among conifers and open slopes; no lake or stream beside any site (Ditch Creek runs well south-east of the loop) -> not waterfront.
fees_source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r04/bridger-teton/recreation/camping-cabins ('Dispersed camping (outside campgrounds) is free'; Shadow Mountain row lists no fee, first come, first served), read 2026-11-20

booking.note: 5-night limit May 1 through Labor Day (Order 04-03-24-204, all of Jackson RD); 14 nights in 30 the rest of the year. Camping only at the marked, designated sites.

booking_source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r04/bridger-teton/recreation/camping-cabins ('No. First come, first served.'; 'camping is permitted only at marked, designated sites'; 14 days within any 30-day period forest-wide) + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r04/bridger-teton/alerts/camping-5-day-stay-limit-jackson-blackrock-big-piney-greys-river-ranger (Order 04-03-24-204: Described Area A 'All NFS lands within the Jackson Ranger District' five days in 30 May 1 - Labor Day; Area D 'Shadow Mountain ... designated camping areas within Jackson Ranger District' camping restricted to designated sites) + recreation.gov search (no listing), read 2026-11-20
hookups_source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r04/bridger-teton/recreation/camping-cabins ('RV Camping: ... No hookups or dump stations are available, so RVs must be self-contained'), read 2026-11-20
facilities_source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r04/bridger-teton/recreation/camping-cabins (Shadow Mountain row: 'Toilet at base. No water.'; 'No hookups or dump stations are available'), read 2026-11-20; The Dyrt review 2026-07-16: 'have installed vault toilets at the base of the mountain'
flags: ROAD LAYER (as asked): USFS EDW_RoadBasic_01 (queried 2026-11-20) codes the main road FR 30340 SHADOW MOUNTAIN (7.14 mi, the summit loop) at maintenance level '3 - SUITABLE FOR PASSENGER CARS', 'Gravel Road, Suitable for Passenger Car'. Its short spurs 30340A-F (0.09-0.44 mi each), 30345 'SHADOW MOUNTIAN' (0.3 mi) and 30345A are level '2 - HIGH CLEARANCE VEHICLES'. So the ML2 rule does not reach every site: the base lot (the pin) opens straight off the ML3 road at its first hairpin, and the loop's own pull-outs are on ML3. Sites down the ML2 spurs may need clearance; the note steers larger rigs to the base sites.

ACCESS WORDING: the FS says only 'Summit loop road is rough in places' - no RV, trailer, 4WD or high-clearance statement and no rig limit (unlike its 30-ft limits on Curtis Canyon and Toppings Road). Campers: 'If it rained 4x4 is needed' (2025-09), 'the top of the road is a mudpit' when wet (2025-06), a 30-ft RV/trailer 'struggling' on the initial climb (2024-07), a 26-ft Class C 'made it up to #18 fine' (2024-07). The Dyrt's auto-generated FAQ says 'Four-wheel drive is highly recommended' and 'large RVs are not advised' - not an agency statement, so weather-conditional caveat only. Reviewer may prefer a skip if the camper reports should weigh.
SITE COUNT not written: no agency count; camper reports range from '20 something' (2025) to '51 numbered sites' (2026-07).
PIN: the base gravel loop with the toilet building (imagery shows trailers parked there), not a summit site.
SEASON from the MVUM road dates (05-01 to 11-30), not a stated campground season; drop it if the reviewer wants only campground wording.
Campendium (refuses, 403) was not opened; its per-site pages were seen only as search titles.
